subject: Biotechnology
title: Biogas from Organic Waste
description: A fast breakdown of Biogas from Organic Waste for builders.

hook.text: One ton of food waste produces 200 cubic meters of biogas — enough electricity to power a home for two weeks.

buildup.text: Anaerobic digestion breaks organic waste into methane and CO2 — four microbial groups work in sequence to complete the conversion.

discovery.text: Digestate, the solid residue, is a nutrient-rich fertilizer — anaerobic digestion produces both energy and soil amendment.

twist.text: Contamination with plastics and glass disrupts digestion — source separation of food waste is essential for clean biogas.

climax.text: Seoul captures biogas from all food waste citywide — converting 5,000 tons per day into vehicle fuel and heating.

punchline.text: Yesterday's leftovers power today's lights — food waste biogas is urban renewable energy.

quiz.question: What are the two main products of anaerobic digestion of food waste?
options: Methane-rich biogas for energy and nutrient-rich digestate for fertilizer

details.summary: Biogas production uses anaerobic digestion by methanogenic archaea and bacteria to convert organic waste into methane and carbon dioxide. Agricultural waste, food scraps, and sewage become renewable fuel for electricity generation, heating, and vehicle fuel after upgrading to biomethane.
details.whyItMatters: Biogas simultaneously solves two problems: waste disposal and renewable energy production. It diverts organic waste from landfills while generating carbon-neutral fuel, making it a key technology in the circular bioeconomy and climate change
takeaways: Anaerobic digestion converts organic waste into methane-rich biogas
Biogas can generate electricity, heat, or be upgraded to pipeline-quality biomethane
It diverts organic waste from landfills while producing renewable energy

faq.question: What can be used as feedstock for biogas production?
faq.answer: Almost any organic material works: food waste, animal manure, crop residues, sewage sludge, and energy crops. Co-digestion mixing multiple feedstocks often improves gas yield and process stability. Lignocellulosic materials require pretreatment to be efficiently digested.

faq.question: How does biogas compare to fossil natural gas?
faq.answer: Raw biogas is about 50 to 70 percent methane compared to over 90 percent for natural gas. After upgrading to remove CO2 and impurities, biomethane is chemically identical to natural gas and can enter existing pipelines. It is carbon-neutral because the CO2 released was recently captured by plants.
